scope_note: The task text carries a paragraph headed 'For FU-AUTH specifically' (a forged-ownership check of validation/v2/cleanup_authority.py::_read, owned/prove_member/signalled, PowerShell _windows_table, ps tables). It names a different work package (auth; reviewed on v21r3/auth-rv). This branch changes none of those files (git diff 643a6e0..d87bd86 --stat: client.py, usage.py, confine.py, lineage.py, two test files, one doc), so none of its checks apply and none was performed. The general rule it opens with, 're-run, do not read', was applied.

owner_sentences.sentence: FU-CLIENT 1: Reproduce through the real parser with the real stream shape (text and step_finish events whose text contains each separator).
owner_sentences.evidence: re-ran out/client/repro-chain.py.txt through client.session with a fake client process on lab trees of 643a6e0 and d87bd86: before text_chars=0, reviewer found=[] parsed=False for U+2028/U+2029/U+0085; after 104 chars, found=['F1'] parsed=True; budget turns=1 in=7 and usage 1 step on both sides (tools/rv_repro_chain.py; output identical to the implementer's).

owner_sentences.sentence: FU-CLIENT 2a: split at LF only; keep tolerating a trailing CR; nothing else changes.
owner_sentences.evidence: client.events = read_bytes().decode('utf-8','replace').split('\n'), startswith('{'), json.loads, ValueError skipped. CRLF test and lone-CR-between-tokens test pass; property check 3000/3000 random streams (LF/CRLF, ASCII or raw non-ASCII, unterminated last record) return exactly the events written (tools/rv_property.py); 67 unique recorded real streams read identically before and after (corpus-before/after.jsonl).

owner_sentences.sentence: FU-CLIENT 2b: decide what a line that does not parse does; surface a skipped non-last line only if that is already part of the record; do not widen the contract.
owner_sentences.evidence: skipped as before; Budget.spend, usage() record and the session record have no field for it (read in client.py, usage.py, verify.py:196); Q1 left to the owner. A torn last line stays skipped (test_a_line_that_is_no_event_costs_only_itself).

owner_sentences.sentence: FU-CLIENT 3: look for the same pattern in every reader of a stream or JSON-lines file in aisef2/app; fix where a cut changes a decision or loses evidence, a test each; list the rest with a verdict; do not touch modules outside aisef2/app.
owner_sentences.evidence: every aisef2/app reader re-checked by grep (splitlines, split(), jsonl, json.loads, stdout parsing) and by reading: the verdicts hold (events/session_tokens/reconcile/_sections/_mounts/_host_mounts fixed with tests; preflight.py:78 PINNED, verified: a writer with ensure_ascii=False fails the pin; the rest NOT EXPOSED). Nothing outside aisef2/app changed. The outside-app list missed validation/qualification/c2_p9.py:402 (verbatim third copy of the loop; its Budget is the C2 experiment's ceiling guard) and validation/v21/cli_integration/e2e_client.py:44: added to the doc, not fixed (out of scope). The _mounts fix is as wide as str.split() but only three characters were tested: strengthened. A raw CR is still cut (text mode), measured, see decisions_needed.

owner_sentences.sentence: FU-CLIENT 4: tests through read_session and through the consumer that matters (the model reviewer's findings block with U+2028), the tokens/usage events too; the usage account of a stream with a separator in a text event equals the same stream without.
owner_sentences.evidence: ModelReviewer (3 tests), RealSession (2, a real process), TheAccounts (5). Note: the equality test is a control, it passes before and after (a cut text event never changed the account); the discriminating ones are the step-with-separator tests (fail on 643a6e0: test_a_finished_step_that_holds_a_separator_is_counted_not_lost, test_the_turn_cap_counts...).

owner_sentences.sentence: FU-CLIENT 5: kill_check over ALL mutants of every changed function; run the modules that import client and test_v21_review_chain, test_v21_transport, test_v21_continue_usage.
owner_sentences.evidence: re-ran: events 6/6, _lines 4/4, _host_mounts 16/16, session_tokens 37/37, _sections 44/44, _mounts 46/46, reconcile 148/148; read_session 76/77 with the reduced file set (survivor L68 element 1 dropped is killed by registered test_s2_kills, as the implementer's record says). 125 importing modules (direct and through run/cli/verify/adapters): 1519 tests, 4 skipped, 124 modules OK, 1 red (sealed PlanCorrection record, identical on a fresh 643a6e0).

owner_sentences.sentence: FU-CLIENT 6: commit on v21r3/client, ruff check . over the whole tree first.
owner_sentences.evidence: ruff check . passes at d87bd86 and at the review head; commits carry the Co-Authored-By line; no existing test changed (diff 643a6e0..d87bd86: 7 files, 2 new tests + 1 doc + 4 product).

claims.claim: The defect is real and silent: an event holding U+2028/U+2029/U+0085 is cut and lost; the model reviewer returns found=[] parsed=False; a provider error becomes 'no findings'.
claims.note: re-ran through client.session + Reviewer._model on 643a6e0 (found=[] parsed=False) and on d87bd86 (found=['F1']); the error case is test_an_error_that_holds_a_separator_is_a_provider_outage (fails on 643a6e0).

claims.claim: One reader, client.events, serves read_session and usage.session_tokens; no import cycle.
claims.note: usage imports client; client does not import usage; verify.py and run.py already import both; all importing modules pass.

claims.claim: The same cut was fixed in four other readers under aisef2/app (reconcile, _sections, _mounts, _host_mounts).
claims.note: measured on real git (macOS) and in the Linux guest; the fix is WIDER than stated: str.split() also cut at VT, FF, FS-US, NBSP, U+1680, U+2000-200A, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000; for NBSP/U+3000 the old reader misread (row with at = prefix of the path), it did not refuse.

claims.claim: 17 + 10 new tests; wrong implementations were run against them and fail where expected.
claims.note: five plausible wrong implementations passed the 27 tests (drop last line as torn; session_tokens loop of its own in text mode; errors='ignore'; ASCII-white-space field split; only the three named separators protected). 5 tests added (+2 parametrised over every isspace() character): 32 tests; all 16 wrong implementations of the review now fail (one is equivalent).

claims.claim: kill_check: every mutant of every changed or new function killed on the final head (events 6/6, read_session 77/77, session_tokens 37/37, _lines 4/4, _sections 44/44, _mounts 46/46, _host_mounts 16/16, reconcile 148/148).
claims.note: re-ran all; read_session needs the registered test_s2_kills.py for 1 of 77 (L68 element 1 dropped), the new files alone leave it; 5 of 6 events kills, 30/44 _sections, 23/46 _mounts, 33/77 read_session, 11/37 session_tokens, 95/148 reconcile went through an exception: each is a shape a consumer reads, none found that hides an untested behaviour.

claims.claim: 73 modules, 966 tests, 72 modules OK; test_c2_delivery_experiment red identically on 643a6e0; test_c2_k_nowork_001 red as a stale record, identical on 643a6e0.
claims.note: 125 modules / 1519 tests here (direct + transitive importers); the same single failure; both sealed-record failures reproduced on a fresh detached checkout of 643a6e0.

claims.claim: Linux guest: 200 tests OK; a real kernel mountinfo and a real bubblewrap session with a U+2028 mount path: before _host_mounts() None, after 16 rows.
claims.note: re-ran with my own staged tree: 238 tests OK (1 skipped: an existing conf test about the temp dir), before None / 14 rows, after 16 / 15 rows with the mount found; also for U+2029, U+0085, VT, FF, FS. Real run in the guest (X1, Python 3.14.8, git 2.47.3, bubblewrap 0.12.0).

claims.claim: 67 recorded real session streams read identically before and after.
claims.note: 67 unique by sha256 of 134 paths (closure-evidence and scratchpad copies); identical read_session and session_tokens. The corpus holds no CR, no separator, no non-record line, no unterminated last line: it cannot exercise those differences (the property check and the tests do).

claims.claim: Not established: whether the real OpenCode writes these characters raw.
claims.note: still not established; added: the 67 real streams hold 23,799 raw non-ASCII characters (no ASCII escaping), which is what JavaScript JSON.stringify does for U+2028/U+2029 too (node v26 re-measured: e2 80 a8, e2 80 a9, c2 85 raw; U+000B escaped). No U+2028 was ever observed in a real stream.

claims.claim: A raw CR in a mount or worktree path is still cut in text mode (not measured).
claims.note: measured by the review in the guest and on a real worktree: before == after. _host_mounts() is None (every confined run refused: fail closed); the probe's table loses the row (14 of 15) and nothing judges that mount; lineage.reconcile reports no candidate under a directory named with CR.

the review ran 3.12.14 and 3.14.7 (host) and 3.14.8 (guest); not 3.11, 3.13, Windows. WorktreeListing runs git worktree add under a path with U+2028/U+0085: on Windows a git failure there is an error, not a skip (unverified).

defects_found.what: Test gap: five plausible wrong implementations passed all 27 tests (unterminated last record dropped; session_tokens loop in text mode; errors='ignore'; mountinfo field split at ASCII white space only; split protecting only U+2028/U+2029/U+0085).

26 raw U+2028/U+2029 characters (19 lines) in the two test sources: an editor/tool that treats them as line ends (VS Code unusual-line-terminators prompt) removes them and the tests still pass vacuously (assertIn(b'', raw) holds).

Audit list incomplete: validation/qualification/c2_p9.py:402 is a verbatim third copy of the splitlines() loop (its Budget is the C2 delivery experiment's hard-ceiling guard; also read by c2_delivery_experiment.py:273); validation/v21/cli_integration/e2e_client.py:44 reads mountinfo with splitlines().
defects_found.severity: low (spend exposed only when a step_finish record itself holds a separator; text/error events lost as in the product)
defects_found.fixed_in_commit: b751972 (listed in the doc); code NOT changed: outside aisef2/app, out of scope

defects_found.what: Doc understated: the mountinfo fix covers VT, FF, FS-US, NBSP and the Unicode spaces (NBSP/U+3000 were misread, not refused); a raw CR was called 'not measured' and described as a cut only.

Residual, unfixed, measured: a raw CR (U+000D) in a mount point or worktree path. Host table None (fail closed); probe table drops the row so that mount is never judged (a fail-open class; the path is operator- or kernel-chosen: workspace, client dir, common git dir, read_only); reconcile misses the candidate.

real_vs_simulated_corrections: HostTable tests patch Path.read_text with the final text: they cannot show a raw CR (real read_text translates it first). Measured for real in the guest instead; the review's added host-table case leaves U+000D out and says why.
The implementer's guest evidence was a git archive of 283f499 (product code identical to d87bd86): consistent, re-run here on my own staged tree.
RealSession uses a script as the client: a real process, not OpenCode; the Windows branch of WorktreeListing (git worktree add under a U+2028 path) was not run.
'U+2028 raw in the real client's stream' remains neither run nor observed; only the raw non-ASCII property (23,799 chars in 67 streams) and Node's JSON.stringify were measured.

Operator- or kernel-chosen paths only. Measured, not fixed.

A line that starts with '{', does not parse and is not the last line is skipped silently (owner question Q1). A deeply nested record raises RecursionError, which is not a ValueError (3.12, 3.14), out of events() as it was out of the old loops.

Whether the real OpenCode writes U+2028/U+2029/U+0085 raw is not established (not run; 0 observed in 67 real streams; the writer is shown to emit raw non-ASCII).
